Secrets are stored encrypted and are never shown again once written. Connection infrastructure and server credentials are managed only from the environment.

descriptions.keepa.refresh.enabled: Master switch for the background Keepa refresh scheduler. Turning it off stops all background token spend immediately, with no restart needed.
descriptions.keepa.refresh.intervalMinutes: How often the scheduler claims a batch of products to refresh from Keepa. Lower values refresh more often but spend Keepa tokens faster.
descriptions.keepa.refresh.batchSize: How many products are claimed per refresh tick. Batches over 100 are chunked automatically, so this can safely exceed Keepa's per-call limit.
descriptions.keepa.refresh.claimLeaseMinutes: How long a claimed batch is reserved before it becomes due again. Must exceed the worst-case batch runtime including retries, or a product could be claimed twice.
descriptions.keepa.refresh.maxFailures: Number of consecutive data failures (ASIN missing from a Keepa response) before a product is quarantined and stops being refreshed.
descriptions.keepa.refresh.quarantineMinutes: How long a product stays quarantined after hitting the failure threshold before refresh is retried.
descriptions.keepa.refresh.schedulerCron: Cron pattern for the refresh scheduler tick. The repeatable job is registered once at boot, so a change here needs an API restart to take effect.
descriptions.amazon.orderSync.cron: How often each Amazon buyer account is scraped to auto-capture order costs. Cost scales with account count, not sales volume — raising the frequency only speeds up how soon already-placed orders get their real costs written; nothing a seller waits on runs here.
descriptions.amazon.orderSync.matchTolerancePct: Tie-break for automatic cost matching: an Amazon order total within this percentage of the order's expected product cost ranks that eBay order higher. It never blocks a match — the product, quantity, recipient and date decide.
descriptions.amazon.orderSync.matchWindowDays: Maximum number of days allowed between the Amazon and eBay order dates for an automatic cost match.
descriptions.amazon.tracking.preshipIntervalHours: How often an order is polled for a ship-out event before it has shipped. Baked into per-order schedulers at boot — a restart is needed to apply a new value to already-scheduled orders.
descriptions.amazon.tracking.shippedIntervalHours: How often a shipped order is polled for delivery status. Also requires a restart to apply to already-scheduled orders.
descriptions.autoFulfill.reviewCapHardStop: When on, the automated Amazon purchase aborts before clicking 'Place Order' if the review-page total exceeds the buyer account's spend cap.
descriptions.autoFulfill.evidenceTtlDays: How many days full-page evidence screenshots from automated purchases are kept before being deleted.
descriptions.email.smtpHost: Hostname of the SMTP server used to send platform emails.
descriptions.email.smtpPort: Port used to connect to the SMTP server (587 for STARTTLS, 465 for implicit TLS).
descriptions.email.smtpSecure: Use implicit TLS when connecting to the SMTP server.
descriptions.email.smtpUser: Username used to authenticate with the SMTP server.
descriptions.email.smtpPassword: Password used to authenticate with the SMTP server. Stored encrypted and never shown again once set.
descriptions.email.smtpFrom: The From address platform emails are sent from.
descriptions.admin.queueWaitingThreshold: Number of waiting jobs in a queue that triggers a warning on the Overview tab.
descriptions.admin.keepaLowTokensThreshold: Keepa token balance below which a low-balance warning is shown.
descriptions.admin.llmFailureRateThreshold: AI request failure rate (%) above which a warning is shown.
descriptions.admin.listingQuotaWarnThreshold: Number of active listings for a user that triggers a warning-level quota badge.
descriptions.admin.listingQuotaCriticalThreshold: Number of active listings for a user that triggers a critical-level quota badge.
descriptions.admin.amazonAccountQuotaWarnThreshold: Number of Amazon buyer accounts for a user that triggers a warning-level quota badge.
descriptions.admin.amazonAccountQuotaCriticalThreshol: Number of Amazon buyer accounts for a user that triggers a critical-level quota badge.
descriptions.llm.contentEnabled: Master switch for AI-generated listing titles and descriptions at create time. Off by default; a failure always falls back to the deterministic title.
descriptions.billing.enforcementEnabled: When on, listing and automatic-order quotas are actually enforced against a user's plan. Off gives every user full access without a real subscription.
descriptions.buyerMessaging.feedbackDefaultDelayDays: Default number of days after delivery before the feedback-request message is sent, when a store hasn't set its own delay.
descriptions.amazon.browserProfileGc.enabled: Master switch for the nightly cleanup of Amazon browser profiles — cache pruning and disk reclaim for unused or orphaned accounts.
descriptions.amazon.browserProfileGc.dormantDays: Days a browser profile can sit unused before it is fully removed, forcing a re-login on next use. Set to 0 to disable full removal while keeping cache pruning.
descriptions.amazon.browserProfileGc.purgeOrphans: Remove browser profiles belonging to Amazon accounts that no longer exist in the database.
descriptions.retention.queueObservationsDays: How many days of BullMQ queue completed/failed event history are kept.
descriptions.retention.keepaUsageLogDays: How many days of per-ASIN Keepa token usage log rows are kept.
descriptions.retention.llmUsageLogDays: How many days of AI usage log rows (tokens, cost) are kept.
descriptions.retention.usageEventsDays: How many days of the FinOps cost-projection table that feeds the Costs tab are kept.
descriptions.retention.buyerMessageLogDays: How many days buyer message log rows are kept. This table also prevents duplicate messages for the same order/event — deleting a row re-arms that event, so the floor is deliberately long.
descriptions.retention.auditLogsDays: How many days audit log rows (role changes, setting changes) are kept. Kept long for compliance evidence.
descriptions.retention.listingRevisionsDays: How many days of listing revision history are kept for the detail page's Revisions drawer.
descriptions.retention.bestSellersViewsDays: How many days of the Best Sellers view ledger are kept. The sum of this table over the current billing period IS the seller's used product allowance, so the floor stays well above one billing period; older rows are browsing history only.
descriptions.retention.ebayNotificationEventsDays: How many days of received eBay NEW_MESSAGE notifications are kept. Only used to ignore eBay's retried deliveries, which stop after 3 attempts.
descriptions.retention.ebayNotificationRawCapturesDay: How many days of verbatim eBay notification requests are kept for diagnosing signature or payload problems.
descriptions.retention.autoFulfillEventsDays: How many days the step-by-step record of automatic Amazon purchases is kept. It is the evidence used to investigate a duplicate or a missing purchase; nothing reads it to make a decision.
descriptions.ebay.aspects.llmEnabled: Allow the AI to choose a required eBay item specific when no cheaper deterministic layer could supply one. Off by default.
descriptions.ebay.aspects.llmMaxPerListing: Maximum number of item specifics the AI is allowed to resolve per listing when the AI aspect layer is enabled.
descriptions.keepa.refresh.batchAuto: When on, the batch size is calculated from the Keepa plan's own refill rate, so upgrading the plan raises throughput on its own. Turn off to use the fixed batch size value.
descriptions.keepa.refresh.reservePercent: The share of the Keepa token rate that background refresh leaves unused, so tokens remain when a seller adds listings. Applies only while automatic batch sizing is on.
descriptions.ebay.budget.enabled: eBay calls for every seller are drawn from a single daily quota. When on, each call is counted and work is deferred to the next day once the quota is spent. When off nothing is counted and only eBay's own error limits it.
descriptions.ebay.budget.reservePercent: This share of each quota is kept for actions a seller starts themselves, such as publishing a listing. Background jobs running overnight cannot use it.
descriptions.ebay.returnSync.enabled: Periodically read each store's return requests from eBay so the Returns page and its deadlines stay current. Turning it off freezes the Returns page.
descriptions.ebay.finances.billingSync.enabled: Every few hours, read the billing activity of each store that granted the Finances permission and save it to disk as it came, so the real ad fees can be learned. Nothing is written to the database. Stores without the permission are never read.
descriptions.ebay.finances.billingSync.cron: How often the sweep looks for due stores (cron). How often one store is read is the interval below. Applied after a restart.
descriptions.ebay.finances.billingSync.intervalHours: Hours between two reads of the same store. The Finances API allows 15,000 calls a day for the whole platform; 4 hours keeps 500 stores well inside it.
descriptions.ebay.finances.billingSync.maxAccountsPer: How many due stores one tick reads, one after another. A burst guard only.
descriptions.ebay.finances.billingSync.windowDays: How many days of billing activity each read asks eBay for. eBay allows at most 120.
descriptions.ebay.returnSync.cron: How often more stores are picked up. Read once at boot.
descriptions.ebay.returnSync.intervalAuto: Work out how often each store's returns are read from the number of active stores and eBay's daily limit, so the quota is never exceeded: about every hour with a few stores, every 6 hours at 500. Turn off to use the manual value below.
descriptions.ebay.returnSync.quotaPercent: How much of eBay's daily return quota the sweep may spend (default 50). A higher share reads returns more often; the rest is kept for retries.
descriptions.ebay.returnSync.intervalHours: Used only when the automatic interval is off, or before eBay has reported a limit (default 6). eBay allows 5,000 return calls a day for all sellers together, and each sweep costs one per store.
descriptions.ebay.returnSync.maxAccountsPerRun: The most stores one run reads (default 35). A burst limit only; the interval decides the pace.
descriptions.ebay.returns.actionsEnabled: Let sellers approve a return, mark the returned item as received and issue the refund from the Returns page. These eBay calls move real money and cannot be tried in Sandbox: switch on after the first real return has been handled through SellerHill successfully. Off = every return is answered on eBay.
descriptions.listing.cleanup.enabled: Master switch for the sellers' own clean-up rules: ending listings that stayed out of stock, or did not sell, for the number of days a seller chose. Each seller's rule is off until they turn it on. Off here stops every automatic ending at once without changing anyone's settings.
descriptions.ebay.feedSync.enabled: Periodically ask eBay which listings still exist, so a listing ended on eBay stops being treated as live here. Off by default.
descriptions.ebay.oauth.financesScopeEnabled: Adds eBay's sell.finances scope to the consent screen, so a store connected or reconnected afterwards lets SellerHill read the ad fees eBay charged. Stores connected before must reconnect once. Turn it off if eBay starts refusing consents.
descriptions.ebay.feedSync.captureOnly: Download the report and change nothing — it is written to disk so its format can be confirmed against a real store. Leave on until the report parser ships.
descriptions.ebay.feedSync.cron: How often more stores are picked up. Read once at boot.
descriptions.ebay.feedSync.intervalHours: How long before the same store is reconciled again (default 24).
descriptions.ebay.feedSync.maxAccountsPerRun: How many stores each run reconciles. Keep low: eBay limits how many report tasks may run at once and does not publish the figure.
descriptions.tracking.aquiline.baseUrl: Base address of the tracking-number conversion provider's Integration API. You should not need to change it.
descriptions.tracking.aquiline.apiKey: In the form tokenId.tokenSecret. Stored encrypted and never shown again once written. While empty, tracking conversion cannot run and shipments are held instead of being sent to eBay.
descriptions.tracking.aquiline.timeoutMs: The longest each call to the provider may take (default 15000).
descriptions.tracking.aquiline.webhookSecret: Issued once by Aquiline when the webhook is registered; used to verify the signature on incoming notifications. Stored encrypted. If wrong or empty, every notification is rejected.
descriptions.tracking.aquiline.webhookMaxAgeMinutes: Signed notifications older than this are treated as replays and rejected (default 1440, i.e. 24 hours).
descriptions.tracking.aquiline.profilePrefix: Name prefix for the seller profiles created at Aquiline (default sh). One Aquiline account serves every environment, so this keeps environments apart.
descriptions.tracking.aquiline.maxProfiles: The number of seller profiles your Aquiline plan allows (Starter 10; then 25, 50, 100, 250). Raise it here when you upgrade the plan. Profiles are permanent and cannot be deleted.
descriptions.billing.trialDays: The free trial given to a newly registered seller, between 1 and 90. A change applies only to sellers who register after it is saved.
descriptions.billing.webhookGraceHours: How long to wait after a subscription period ends, if the renewal notification is late, before the account is suspended (default 6). A paying seller is not interrupted at the renewal moment.
descriptions.llm.apiKey: The AI provider's API key. Stored encrypted and never shown again once written. If the panel holds no value, the LLM_API_KEY environment variable is used. With no key, AI title and item-specific writing does not run and listings still open with the normal title. The provider address and model are managed only from the environment, for security.
descriptions.product.dataProvider: Where Amazon product data comes from. "scraper" is our own service; "keepa" is the rollback. The two never mix.
descriptions.scraper.proxies: Add each proxy on its own row (http, https, socks5 or socks5h). Test a row before saving. Without any proxy, no Amazon data is fetched — the server's own IP is never used.
descriptions.scraper.perIpRequestsPerSecond: How fast each proxy may fetch pages. Each proxy runs enough workers for this rate; total throughput ≈ rate × proxies while Amazon answers within ~2 s.
descriptions.scraper.inStockFloor: Stock recorded when Amazon shows "In Stock" without a count. Displayed as N+.
descriptions.scraper.blockRateWarnPercent: Admin warning when this share of scraper requests was blocked in the last hour.
descriptions.bestSellers.enabled: Lets sellers browse Amazon's Best Sellers lists in the app. Off hides the page and refuses the endpoint; the lists are fetched through the scraper proxies, never the server's own IP.
descriptions.bestSellers.cacheTtlMinutes: How long a fetched list page is served to every seller before it is fetched again. Longer saves proxy capacity; Amazon updates the lists about hourly.
descriptions.bestSellers.dailyFetchLimit: Platform anti-abuse cap, hidden from sellers: how many LIVE list fetches (cache misses) one seller may trigger per UTC day before the page answers 429. Cache hits are free. This is NOT the seller allowance — that is the plan's Best Sellers products per billing period, which locks rows instead of refusing. Keep it far above real use; 0 stops live fetches for everyone while cached pages keep serving.
descriptions.bestSellers.crawl.enabled: Reads Amazon's whole category tree for all five lists in the background, so any branch a seller expands opens instantly. Runs only on capacity the price/stock refresh leaves idle, and never without a scraper proxy. Off stops the crawl; what is cached keeps serving.
descriptions.bestSellers.crawl.intervalDays: A category is read again once its stored copy is older than this, and a new pass over the tree starts no more often. Categories change over months; keep it below 14 days, the life of a stored copy.
descriptions.bestSellers.crawl.pagesPerMinute: Tree pages read per minute (one request each, no products). About 250,000 pages make up the five lists; 30 a minute finishes a pass in under six days. 0 pauses the crawl.
descriptions.bestSellers.prewarm.depth: Deepest level whose Best Sellers product list is fetched ahead of sellers, every list-cache period: 0 = the main page, 1 = departments, 2 = their sub-categories (about 900 lists).
descriptions.bestSellers.prewarm.pagesPerMinute: Product lists the pre-warm fetches per minute (about four requests each). 3 a minute covers depth 2 within one 6-hour cache period. 0 turns the pre-warm off.

ebayLimits.description: eBay meters API calls per application, not per seller - every customer draws from one daily pool. The limits come from eBay itself; nobody sets them here. Background jobs stop at the reduced ceiling so seller-triggered actions always have budget left.
ebayLimits.noEbayFigure: eBay reports no daily limit - not gated
ebayLimits.compareHint: eBay's day and ours reset at different times, so compare the two counts by eye. Our count far below eBay's usage means some call is bypassing the budget.
ebayLimits.figuresStale: Could not reach eBay just now - showing the last figures it gave.
ebayLimits.figuresMissing: eBay has not reported its limits yet, so nothing is being gated. Calls are still counted.
ebayLimits.unmappedDescription: Everything eBay meters that the budget does not govern, shown so a mapping that stops matching is visible.
ebayLimits.emptyDescription: Rows appear once eBay reports its limits or the platform makes its first eBay call today.

listingFailures.description: Operator diagnostics. Sellers only ever see the localized reason; the raw provider message is shown here because it names eBay error ids and internal fields.
listingFailures.emptyDescription: Failed create attempts appear here with the raw provider error.

vero.title: VeRO brand list
vero.hint: Brand names refused for every seller who keeps VeRO protection on. Matched against a product's brand and manufacturer only, as whole words. Sellers never see this list — only the one brand that stopped a product of theirs.
vero.addPlaceholder: Brand names, one per line or separated by commas
vero.addResult: Added: {{added}}. Already on the list or blank: {{skipped}}.
vero.addFailed: The brand names could not be added. Try again.
vero.empty: The list is empty, so VeRO protection refuses nothing yet.
